endorsements.quote: Studies should document split construction and data provenance, align validation with the intended test condition, and prevent test information from entering model development.

Aggregate performance should also be accompanied by worst-domain or lower-quantile performance, domain-level uncertainty intervals, and calibration across domains or shift-severity strata [ 42 ].
Performance should be reported for individual domains and summarized across domains.

unlisted_practices: Report the applicable L0-L5 evaluation setting or combination of settings together with quantitative measures of the resulting train-test discrepancy.
Audit the train-test discrepancy using coverage, overlap, and distance, independently of model performance, specifying the representation, metric, and aggregation used.
Accompany cold-start protocols with an operational description of what is withheld and any additional structural, temporal, or domain constraints.
Disclose potential leakage from external resources, pretrained representations, graph features, or temporal information.
Provide reproducibility materials including entity lists, candidate-pair universes, split identifiers, group assignments, data versions, seeds, and reconstruction code.
Define candidate pair universe and label semantics, including negative sampling, duplicate, reverse, and self-pair handling, and class prevalence.
Do not treat an evaluation label as a proxy for the magnitude of distribution shift.

screen.reason: This is a perspective piece proposing a framework and checklist (recommendations) for auditable cold-start evaluation and deployment claims in drug-drug and drug-target interaction models.
